title: Replay and Ripples: Correlation to Perturbation

scenes.tts: Could a group of cells that completes itself also be set going while the animal rests?
scenes.visual: Title fades. The lit cluster of cells from the first film, with a sleeping rat beside it. The cluster flickers on with no outside cue. On screen: Can the group be set going offline?
scenes.narration: Could a group of cells that completes itself also be set going while the animal rests?

scenes.tts: One proposal: the hippocampus replays experience afterwards, teaching the cortex.
scenes.visual: Schematic brain: an arrow loops from the hippocampus to the cortex, labelled replay. Label: one proposal.
scenes.narration: One proposal: the hippocampus replays experience afterwards, teaching the cortex.

scenes.tts: The evidence moves up the lesson's ladder: from correlation to turning ripple activity off.
scenes.visual: The lesson's ladder: correlation on the bottom rung; on the rung above, two intervention tests side by side at equal height, sufficiency (turn on) and necessity (turn off). Correlation and necessity are outlined for this film.
scenes.narration: The evidence moves up the lesson's ladder: from correlation to turning ripple activity off.

scenes.tts: Matthew Wilson and Bruce McNaughton recorded many hippocampal cells at once in three rats.
scenes.visual: Name card: Wilson and McNaughton, 1994. Three rat icons, each with a bundle of recording wires.
scenes.narration: Matthew Wilson and Bruce McNaughton recorded many hippocampal cells at once in three rats.

scenes.tts: They compared sleep before a spatial task, the task itself, and sleep after it.
scenes.visual: A timeline in three blocks: sleep before, task, sleep after. Above each block, a bar shows how strongly one pair of task-active cells fires together. Corner label: made-up numbers for teaching. Bars read 0.02, 0.30, 0.10.
scenes.narration: They compared sleep before a spatial task, the task itself, and sleep after it.

scenes.tts: Pairs that co-fired in the task co-fired more in the sleep after it than before.
scenes.visual: The sleep-after bar glows, taller than the sleep-before bar. Arrow from task bar to sleep-after bar.
scenes.narration: Pairs that co-fired in the task co-fired more in the sleep after it than before.

scenes.tts: Pairs that were silent in the task showed no such rise.
scenes.visual: A second row of bars for task-silent pairs: low and equal before and after (0.02 and 0.02).
scenes.narration: Pairs that were silent in the task showed no such rise.

scenes.tts: This was pairwise co-firing, and a correlation, not a test of memory.
scenes.visual: Label over the bars: pairwise co-firing. The correlation rung of the ladder lights.
scenes.narration: This was pairwise co-firing, and a correlation, not a test of memory.

scenes.tts: Later work read the order. Each row here is one place cell, sorted along the track.
scenes.visual: A raster: rows of place cells stacked by field position along a track drawn at the left; ticks mark spikes.
scenes.narration: Later work read the order. Each row here is one place cell, sorted along the track.

scenes.tts: During a run, the spikes form a diagonal, cell after cell.
scenes.visual: As a rat runs the track, ticks appear in a diagonal from bottom left to top right.
scenes.narration: During a run, the spikes form a diagonal, cell after cell.

scenes.tts: In pauses at the end of a run, the sequence replayed in reverse, compressed in time.
scenes.visual: The rat pauses at the track end. The same diagonal replays squeezed into a narrow time window, running top to bottom (reverse). Name card: Diba and Buzsaki, 2007.
scenes.narration: In pauses at the end of a run, the sequence replayed in reverse, compressed in time.

scenes.tts: Before runs, it played forward.
scenes.visual: With the rat at the start of the track, a squeezed diagonal runs forward, bottom to top.
scenes.narration: Before runs, it played forward.

scenes.tts: Much replay rides on sharp-wave ripples, in the local field potential: the summed electrical signal from cells near an electrode.
scenes.visual: An electrode in CA1 with many cells around it; a wavy trace scrolls beneath, labelled local field potential (LFP).
scenes.narration: Much replay rides on sharp-wave ripples, in the local field potential: the summed electrical signal from cells near an electrode.

scenes.tts: A sharp-wave ripple is a slower sharp wave carrying a burst of very fast ripple waves. It lasts tens of milliseconds.
scenes.visual: The trace zooms in on one event: a slow dip labelled sharp wave, with fast oscillations riding on it labelled ripple. On screen: roughly 150 to 250 waves per second; tens of milliseconds.
scenes.narration: A sharp-wave ripple is a slower sharp wave carrying a burst of very fast ripple waves. It lasts tens of milliseconds.

scenes.tts: A computer can detect each ripple as it starts, and trigger a stimulus that cuts it short.
scenes.visual: Closed-loop diagram: trace, detector box, stimulator. A ripple starts, the detector flashes, a stimulus pulse ends the ripple early.
scenes.narration: A computer can detect each ripple as it starts, and trigger a stimulus that cuts it short.

scenes.tts: Rats given this in sleep after training do worse next day. What control do you need before blaming the lost ripples?
scenes.visual: Next-day performance bar for the ripple-cut group, lower than normal. A second, empty slot labelled control, with a question mark. On screen: What control do you need?
scenes.narration: Rats given this in sleep after training do worse next day. What control do you need before blaming the lost ripples?

scenes.tts: Give another group the same stimuli, each delayed after a ripple, so its ripples run their course.
scenes.visual: Second closed-loop diagram: the stimulus pulse lands after a delay, and the ripple finishes intact. Label: delayed control, same number of stimuli.
scenes.narration: Give another group the same stimuli, each delayed after a ripple, so its ripples run their course.

scenes.tts: Gabrielle Girardeau and colleagues did this. Only the ripple-cut group was impaired.
scenes.visual: Name card: Girardeau and colleagues, 2009. Bars fill in: ripple-cut group lower; delayed group normal.
scenes.narration: Gabrielle Girardeau and colleagues did this. Only the ripple-cut group was impaired.

scenes.tts: So the stimulation alone does not explain the deficit. Its timing does: hitting the ripples.
scenes.visual: Note beside both bars: same stimuli, different timing. The ripple label glows. The necessity half of the upper rung lights, labelled ripple activity turned off.
scenes.narration: So the stimulation alone does not explain the deficit. Its timing does: hitting the ripples.

scenes.tts: Another group went the other way. Prolonging ripples in awake rats improved maze working memory.
scenes.visual: Name card: Fernandez-Ruiz and colleagues, 2019. A ripple on the trace stretches longer. A maze icon with a performance bar that rises.
scenes.narration: Another group went the other way. Prolonging ripples in awake rats improved maze working memory.

scenes.tts: That tested awake ripples, not consolidation during sleep.
scenes.visual: Label beside the maze: awake, working memory, not sleep consolidation.
scenes.narration: That tested awake ripples, not consolidation during sleep.

scenes.tts: One limit remains. Cutting ripples removes ripple-linked activity in general, not one route.
scenes.visual: Many replayed sequences sit inside the ripple events; the cut removes all of them together, not one highlighted route.
scenes.narration: One limit remains. Cutting ripples removes ripple-linked activity in general, not one route.

scenes.tts: The ripple evidence climbed from correlation to perturbation. Ripple-linked activity aids memory, in the tasks tested.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Ripple-linked activity aids memory, in the tasks tested.
scenes.narration: The ripple evidence climbed from correlation to perturbation. Ripple-linked activity aids memory, in the tasks tested.
